prompt.en: "Ha Mim Ayn Sin Qaf is the count of the years of the Qa'im, and Qaf is a mountain of green emerald encircling the world." Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked about the disjoined letters, Imam al-Baqir said Ha Mim Ayn Sin Qaf counts the years of the Qa'im and that Qaf is a mountain of green emerald encircling the world.

anchor.quote: Ha Mim Ayn Sin Qaf is the count of the years of the Qa'im, and Qaf is a mountain of green emerald encircling the world

prompt.en: How does Tabatabai read the word 'thus' in 'thus ... reveals to you and to those who were before you'?

options.en: The act of revealing, making revelation a standing practice to every prophet
The surah's meanings, not the act of revealing
God's ownership of the heavens and the earth

explanation.en: Tabatabai reads the surah as an exposition of revelation and takes 'thus' as the act of revealing, so revelation is a standing practice reaching every prophet, not merely the surah's meanings.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai reads the surah as an exposition of revelation, taking 'thus' to point at the act of revealing it, so revelation is a standing practice to every prophet

prompt.en: Tabatabai reads the rending as caused by the revelation descending from the All-high through ____.

explanation.en: Tabatabai explains the rending as the effect of revelation coming down from the All-high, passing through heaven after heaven until it reaches the earth below.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai reads the rending as caused by the revelation descending from the All-high through heaven after heaven

prompt.en: According to the passage, al-Qummi holds the angels' plea for forgiveness is meant for repentant believers among the Shia in particular.

explanation.en: The note says the angels' plea for forgiveness, though worded generally, is meant specifically for the repentant believers among the Shia, which is exactly what the statement claims.

anchor.quote: the forgiveness the angels seek is for the repentant believers among the Shia in particular

prompt.en: According to the essay, what happened after the Yemenis asked to see Sam, son of Noah?

options.en: Sam appeared to them in a dream that night
The Prophet raised Sam before the assembled people
An angel took Sam's form and spoke to them
Ali prayed and struck the ground, and Sam rose from a coffin

explanation.en: The essay reports that when the Yemenis asked to see Sam, son of Noah, Ali prayed and struck the ground, the earth split open, and Sam rose from a coffin.

anchor.quote: al-Burhan carries Ibn Shahr Ashub's report that this came down after Yemenis asked to see Sam, son of Noah: Ali prayed and struck the ground, the earth split open, and Sam rose from a coffin

prompt.en: In the essay, Tabatabai concludes that the one people worship need not be the one who resolves their differences.

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai closes the argument that the guardian who is worshipped must be the very one who resolves people's differences, so God alone is that Lord; the two cannot be split.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai reads this as closing an argument that the guardian who is worshipped must be the one who resolves people's differences, so God alone is that Lord

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, what do the commentators of both traditions read verse 13 to say?

options.en: God prescribed one religion for all the prophets, forbidding division
God gave each prophet a wholly different religion
Only the last prophet received the true religion
The prophets were told to divide into separate paths

explanation.en: The perspectives say the commentators of both traditions read verse 13 in its plain sense: God prescribed one religion for all the prophets and forbade them to divide.

anchor.quote: On verse 13 the commentators of both traditions read the plain sense - God prescribed for all the prophets one religion, forbidding division

prompt.en: "We are those for whom He prescribed His religion ... O family of Muhammad." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Rida reads verse 13 as spoken to the family of Muhammad: they are the ones for whom God prescribed the religion He enjoined upon Noah.

anchor.quote: We are those for whom He prescribed His religion, saying in His Book: 'He has prescribed for you,' O family of Muhammad

prompt.en: According to al-Qummi's note on verse 14, why did the communities split into sects?

options.en: They divided out of ignorance before knowledge reached them
They envied one another over the excellence God gave Amir al-Mu'minin
God had decreed their division from the start
They rejected the Book after inheriting it

explanation.en: Al-Qummi's note says they did not split from ignorance but, after knowledge came, envied and wronged one another over the excellence God gave Amir al-Mu'minin.

anchor.quote: they did not divide out of ignorance, but after the knowledge came they envied and wronged one another over the excellence God gave Amir al-Mu'minin, so they split into sects

prompt.en: The deniers hasten it in ____ while believers are 'apprehensive of it,' and disputers are 'in extreme error.'

explanation.en: The essay says the deniers hasten the Hour in mockery, while the believers are apprehensive of it, so the missing word is mockery.

anchor.quote: The deniers hasten it in mockery while believers are 'apprehensive of it,' and disputers are 'in extreme error.'

prompt.en: In one narration, Imam al-Sadiq treats wealth and children as this world's tillage and a righteous deed as the Hereafter's tillage.

explanation.en: The narration from Imam al-Sadiq draws exactly this line: wealth and children are the tillage of this world, while a righteous deed is the tillage of the Hereafter, and God may join both for some.

anchor.quote: Wealth and children are the tillage of this world, and righteous deed is the tillage of the Hereafter, and God may gather both of them for some peoples.

prompt.en: According to the essay, what does the prior 'conclusive word' do, on al-Tusi's reading?

options.en: It ordains a religion Allah never permitted.
It defers the idolaters' punishment to the Hereafter.
It seals the Prophet's heart against falsehood.
It increases the goodness of every good deed.

explanation.en: The essay, following al-Tusi, explains that the prior conclusive word defers the idolaters' punishment to the Hereafter; without it, judgement would already have fallen between them.

anchor.quote: But for a prior 'conclusive word' by which God defers their punishment to the Hereafter, al-Tusi notes, judgement would already have fallen between them

prompt.en: Performing the good deed is ____ to us, being truthful about us, and that no lie be told against us.

explanation.en: In al-Baqir's narration, doing the good deed of the verse means submission to the Imams, truthfulness about them, and letting no lie be told against them.

anchor.quote: Performing the good deed is submission to us, being truthful about us, and that no lie be told against us.

prompt.en: "He assigns to them angels who strike them with rods - that is the lightning - so they rise." Who said this about the clouds?

explanation.en: Asked about the clouds, Imam Ali described them resting on seashore trees, then driven by a wind, with angels striking them with rods, the lightning, so they rise.

anchor.quote: He assigns to them angels who strike them with rods - that is the lightning - so they rise

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, why does Ibn Kathir doubt the report that the Prophet named 'Fatimah and her children'?

options.en: No companion witnessed the Prophet saying it.
The surah is Meccan and Fatimah then had no children.
It repeats an earlier verse word for word.
The Prophet had forbidden asking any reward at all.

explanation.en: The perspectives note Ibn Kathir doubts the report on historical grounds: the surah is Meccan, and at that time Fatimah had not yet had children, though he still affirms honouring the household.

anchor.quote: doubting it since the surah is Meccan and Fatimah then had no children, while still affirming honour of the household

prompt.en: "There is no throbbing vein, no misfortune, no headache and no illness except by a sin." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq said no ailment befalls a person except by a sin, citing the verse, and added that what God pardons is more than what He calls to account for.

anchor.quote: There is no throbbing vein, no misfortune, no headache and no illness except by a sin

prompt.en: In the essay, what does God's wrecking of the ships mean?

options.en: Stilling the wind so the ships stop
Drowning the passengers for their sins
A reward for the patient and grateful
A warning aimed only at the polytheists

explanation.en: The essay reads God's wrecking of the ships in verse 34 as drowning the passengers for their sins, so that those who dispute His signs learn they have no refuge.

anchor.quote: this is drowning for the passengers' sins

prompt.en: They shun major sins and indecencies, which Tabatabai illustrates with ____, and they forgive when angered

explanation.en: The essay says the believers shun major sins and indecencies, which Tabatabai illustrates with wine, gambling and unchastity, adding that they forgive when angered.

anchor.quote: which Tabatabai illustrates with wine, gambling and unchastity

prompt.en: How does the note on verse 39 describe defending oneself when wronged?

options.en: A duty that admits no refraining
A licence to retaliate beyond the wrong done
A right reserved to the ruler alone
A permission whose holder may act or refrain

explanation.en: The note reads verse 39 as taking redress when wronged, a permission whose holder has the choice: if he wishes he acts, and if he wishes he refrains, not a binding duty.

anchor.quote: it is a permission whose holder has the choice - if he wishes he acts, and if he wishes he refrains

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, al-Tabari holds that the later command to fight abrogated the verse on retaliating after being wronged.

explanation.en: The perspectives say al-Tabari records Ibn Zayd's abrogation claim but rejects it himself, holding the verse on retaliating after being wronged firm and unabrogated.

anchor.quote: Al-Tabari reads it the same way, and records Ibn Zayd's claim that the command to fight later abrogated it, but al-Tabari himself rejects that, holding the verse firm and unabrogated

prompt.en: According to the essay, Tabatabai reads the opening verse as God's response to disbelief and denial, letting such people stray so they never reach the provision He keeps.

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai reads the opening as God's answer to disbelief and denial: having set out the believers' traits, He turns to the others and lets them stray, so they never reach the provision He keeps.

anchor.quote: God's answer to disbelief and denial: having set out the believers' traits, He turns to the others, letting them stray for their disbelief and denial, so they never reach the provision He keeps

prompt.en: 'Humbled by abasement, furtively looking askance' means at the ____.

explanation.en: Imam al-Baqir glosses the wrongdoers' furtive look in this verse as directed at the Qa'im, so the gap is filled by Qa'im.

anchor.quote: 'Humbled by abasement, furtively looking askance' means at the Qa'im

prompt.en: According to the passage, what is the Prophet told his duty is toward those who disregard his warnings?

options.en: To compel them to accept the faith
Only to communicate the message, not to guard their beliefs
To punish them for their denial
To keep count of the deeds they hide

explanation.en: Verse 48 says the Prophet is not sent as their keeper; his duty is only to communicate, and al-Tusi holds his charge is to call them to the truth, not to guard their beliefs.

anchor.quote: the Prophet is told he is no keeper set over them; al-Tusi holds his charge is to call them to the truth, not to guard their beliefs

prompt.en: "Allah pairs the obedient men with houris of paradise, and the obedient women among humans with the obedient men." Who said this?

explanation.en: Glossing 'or He combines them males and females,' Imam al-Hadi said God pairs obedient men with houris and obedient women with obedient men, rebuking a twisted reading that sought a license to sin.

anchor.quote: Allah pairs the obedient men with houris of paradise, and the obedient women among humans with the obedient men

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, how do the Imami narrations read 'We made it a light' and 'you guide to a straight path'?

options.en: The light is Ali, and the Prophet calls to his wilaya
The light is a creature greater than Jibril and Mika'il
The light is the kingdom of the heavens and the earth
The light is the punishment that divides the Garden and Fire

explanation.en: The perspectives say the distinctively Imami layer, al-Qummi's report from al-Baqir, reads the light as Ali and reads 'you guide to a straight path' as commanding his wilaya and calling to it.

anchor.quote: al-Qummi's report from al-Baqir reads the light as Ali and 'you guide to a straight path' as commanding his wilaya and calling to it
